# Meaning as a cognitive representation

I study the cognitive representations that underlie linguistic meaning: the format they take, how they are constructed from linguistic input and context, how they are accessed and used in inference, and how they are retained in memory.

My work combines linguistic theory and experimental psycholinguistics because **theories of representation and theories of processing constrain one another**.

<div class="section-kicker">Research at a glance</div>

## Meaning is represented, constructed, inferred and remembered.

I use linguistic theory to formulate precise hypotheses about meaningful representations, and experimental psycholinguistics to investigate how those representations are built and used. The aim is not to separate theory from processing, but to use each to constrain the other.

:::

[Explore the research →](research/index.html)
:::

### Construction & inference

::: {.concept concept-featured}

### Memory & knowledge

## DPhil students and postdocs

I am interested in working with researchers who want to investigate the cognitive representation of meaning, particularly where linguistic theory and experimental approaches can inform one another.

Projects might concern linguistic representation, incremental interpretation, inference and prediction, memory and knowledge, or related questions at the interface of language and cognition.

[Information about working with me →](people.html)
